message.worldwideblocks.cable.start_gone: The first end no longer exists: connection cancelled.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.cancelled_: Dimension changed: connection cancelled, the cord is free.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.start_take: The first end's port is now in use: connection cancelled.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.result.not: This is not a network device.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.result.inc: This port does not accept this cable.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.result.sam: Pick a device other than the first one.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.result.oth: Both devices must be in the same dimension.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.end_taken: End removed from %s, the other stays on %s, port %s.
message.worldwideblocks.cable.retracted: %s: cable unplugged, the cord is free.
message.worldwideblocks.network.loop: Network loop near %s. Remove one cable of the loop.
item.worldwideblocks.ethernet_cable.tool: Right-click two devices to connect them.
Sneak + click in the air: cancel.
message.worldwideblocks.network.saturate: Network saturated: frames are being lost. Look for a loop.
message.worldwideblocks.network.dhcp_con: Two DHCP servers on the network of %s. Keep only one.
message.worldwideblocks.terminal.busy: %s is in use: one player at the keyboard at a time.
terminal.worldwideblocks.advice.ping.no_: This computer has no route to %s: has it got an address? See "ip addr" and check its cable.
There is no name service in the game yet: give an IPv4 address, such as 192.168.1.1.
terminal.worldwideblocks.advice.ping.hos: No device answered the ARP requests for %s: is it plugged in, and is the address right? See "ip neigh".
terminal.worldwideblocks.advice.ping.net: %s is outside the local network, and the box has no route beyond it yet.
terminal.worldwideblocks.advice.ping.no_: No reply from %s: the requests or the replies were lost on the way. Check the cables.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.intro: Commands of this computer (help <command>: its details):
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.summary.ex: %sends the shell; the next opening starts a new one (Ctrl+D)
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.summary.he: %sthis list, or the details of a command
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.summary.hi: %sthe commands typed (the Up and Down arrows recall them)
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.summary.ip: %sinterfaces, links, routes and neighbours (ip addr, ip route...)
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.summary.pi: %ssends echo requests to an address, until Ctrl+C
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.keys.1: Ctrl+C stops a command. Esc hides the screen; the command goes on.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.keys.2: Shift+Page Up / Page Down or the wheel scroll; Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- size the text.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.clear.1: clear: clears the screen and the lines above it.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.clear.2: clear -x, or Ctrl+L: clears the screen only; scroll up to see what was there.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.exit.1: exit [n]: ends the shell with status n, by default that of the last command.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.exit.2: Ctrl+D on an empty line does the same. The next opening starts a new shell.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.help.1: help [command]: this list, or the details of the commands that start so.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.history.1: history [n]: the commands typed, numbered, or the last n; history -c empties it.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.history.2: As on Debian, a line starting with a space or repeating the last is not kept.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.hostname.1: hostname: the name of this computer, its type and the end of its MAC address.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.hostname.2: Changing it is refused: the account of this computer is not the administrator.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.ip.1: ip addr (ip a), ip addr show eth0: interfaces and addresses. ip link: the links.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.ip.2: ip route: the routes. ip neigh: the addresses found by ARP.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.ip.3: Only these show something; a change (add, del, set...) is not permitted.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.ping.1: ping <address>: a request per second until Ctrl+C; ping -c <n> <address>: n.
terminal.worldwideblocks.help.ping.2: Only the -c option exists, and an address is needed: no name service yet.
